Meta Ads reward ads that solve a problem in 3 seconds flat. Copy this 3-part script for 20% more reach on your next campaign. 
#metaadstips #paidsocial #adcopy #smallbusinessireland
carousels.hook: Meta Ads reward ads that solve a problem in 3 seconds flat
carousels.throughline: Meta’s algorithm favors ads that follow a simple 3-part script—here’s the exact structure to copy.

reel_beats.hook: Your Meta ad reach drops 20% if you skip this script

body.text: Meta’s algorithm looks for ads that solve a problem in 3 clear steps.
The first step names the problem in 5 words or less, so people stop scrolling.
The second step shows the solution in one image—no extra fluff.
The third step tells them exactly what to do next, like ‘Shop now’ or ‘Sign up.’

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to your ad designer

body_slides.text: Part 1: Name the problem in 5 words or less—people stop scrolling.
Part 2: Show the solution in one image—no extra fluff.
Part 3: Tell them exactly what to do next—‘Shop now’ or ‘Sign up.’
Meta’s system rewards ads that guide people from problem to action fast.
Test this script on your next 3 ads—most accounts see 20% more reach.
Save this slide to use as a template for your next ad creative.

carousels.caption:
Google Ads calls 1 in 7 buyers ‘low intent’—they’re not. Fix this one report to save 10-15% of your budget. 
#googleadstips #ppcmanagement #adspend #irishbusiness
carousels.hook: Google Ads calls 1 in 7 buyers ‘low intent’—they’re not
carousels.throughline: Google Ads mislabels 15% of buyers as ‘low intent’—fixing this report saves budget and improves targeting.

reel_beats.hook: Google Ads calls 15% of your buyers ‘low intent’—they’re not

body.text: Google Ads sometimes labels real buyers as ‘low intent’ if they take too long to convert.
This happens because the system only looks at clicks from the last 7 days by default.
Buyers who take 2-4 weeks to decide get ignored, costing you 10-15% of your budget.
Fix it by extending the lookback window to 30 or 60 days in the Attribution tab.

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to your PPC manager

body_slides.text: Google Ads’ ‘conversion value’ report sometimes calls real buyers ‘low intent.’
This happens when the system sees a long gap between click and purchase.
Open the ‘Attribution’ tab and check ‘Time to conversion’ for delays.
Extend the lookback window to 30 or 60 days to catch delayed buyers.
Most accounts save 10-15% of budget after fixing this one setting.
Run this check every month—Google updates its models often.

carousels.caption:
Google Ads hides 1 in 4 of your best leads in plain sight—here’s how to find them in 5 minutes. 
#googleadstips #ppcmanagement #leadgeneration #smallbusinessireland
carousels.hook: Google Ads hides 1 in 4 of your best leads in plain sight
carousels.throughline: Google Ads buries 25% of your best leads in a report most accounts ignore—here’s how to find them.

reel_beats.hook: Google Ads hides 25% of your best leads in a report you’ve never opened

body.text: Google Ads buries high-intent leads in the ‘Search terms’ report under ‘Other searches.’
These are terms with 1-2 clicks that still convert—people who know exactly what they want.
Most accounts waste 20-25% of their budget on broad searches that never convert.
Fix it by adding these terms as exact match keywords and excluding the broad ones.

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to your ads team

body_slides.text: Open the ‘Search terms’ report—most accounts ignore it.
Sort by conversions and look for terms with 1-2 clicks but 1 sale.
These are high-intent leads Google buried in ‘Other searches.’
Add them as exact match keywords to stop wasting budget on broad searches.
Most accounts recover 20-25% of lost sales after this one check.
Run this audit every 2 weeks—new hidden leads appear fast.

carousels.caption:
Gmail moves emails with replies to Primary in hours—here’s how to use that to land in inbox every time. 
#emailmarketingtips #emailcopywriting #conversiontracking #irishbusiness
carousels.hook: Gmail moves emails with replies to Primary in hours
carousels.throughline: Gmail prioritizes emails that spark replies over those with just opens—here’s how to use that to land in Primary.

reel_beats.hook: Gmail buries your email unless someone replies—opens don’t matter

body.text: Gmail’s filter looks for replies, not opens, to decide where your email lands.
Emails that spark replies move to Primary within hours, even with weak subject lines.
Most lists waste 30% of their open rate by not asking for replies.
Fix it by asking a question in the first line and ending with ‘Hit reply.’

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to your email writer

body_slides.text: Gmail’s filter looks for replies, not just opens, to decide inbox placement.
Ask a question in the first line—‘What’s your biggest challenge right now?’
Emails with replies land in Primary within hours, even with weak subject lines.
Test this on your next 3 emails—most lists see 30% more replies.
Use a short, personal sign-off like ‘Hit reply and tell me what you think.’
Gmail rewards engagement—so the more replies, the better your future placement.

carousels.caption:
Meta Ads stop learning if no one converts for 3 days—here’s how to keep your ads improving for weeks. 
#metaadstips #paidsocial #adspend #businessireland
carousels.hook: Meta Ads stop learning if no one converts for 3 days
carousels.throughline: Meta’s algorithm resets your audience after 3 days of inactivity—here’s how to keep it learning longer.

reel_beats.hook: Meta resets your audience after 3 days of silence—your ads stop getting smarter

body.text: Meta’s algorithm assumes your audience is no longer interested if no one converts for 3 days.
This triggers a reset, and your ads start showing to colder audiences again.
Most accounts waste 15% of their budget on this reset before they even notice it.
Fix it by scheduling a small conversion event, like a video view, every 48 hours.

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to your ads manager

body_slides.text: Meta’s system stops learning if no one converts for 3 days straight.
This happens because the algorithm assumes your audience is no longer interested.
Schedule a small conversion event—like a video view—every 48 hours to keep it active.
Use a low-budget ad set just for engagement to signal activity.
Most accounts see 15% better performance after fixing this one gap.
Check your ‘Learning Phase’ status weekly to catch resets early.
